title: Tenant guardrails for retention with anomaly-triggered forensic snapshots and evidence hooks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers operating in regulated environments need retention settings that can both enforce tenant-level TTLs and produce legally defensible evidence when anomalous activity is detected. Current retention features allow per-route TTLs and scheduled evidence exports but lack: a) a lightweight real-time hook to capture short forensic snapshots on anomalies; b) tenant-scoped guardrails that prevent overly permissive TTL overrides by subteams; and c) a signed export artifact (chain-of-custody) that can be triggered automatically and attached to an incident report.

Goal: Deliver a retention guardrail system that: (1) enforces tenant-level minimum/maximum TTLs per artifact type (prompts/responses/request logs/metrics); (2) provides anomaly-triggered forensic snapshot hooks which capture a bounded evidence bundle without changing base retention rules; (3) emits a signed, timestamped evidence package with metadata (route, model, snapshot-reason, trigger-id, tenant-id) to the tenant's evidence S3 bucket or to an automated case export endpoint; (4) surfaces guardrail violations and snapshot activity in Console and via webhook to tenant security teams.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement a full forensic query UI or cryptographic notarization beyond signing with our existing HSM key used by Private deployments. Long-term automated redaction/PII masking flows are out of scope for this incremental delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant-level TTL policy schema defined and persisted (min_ttl_seconds, max_ttl_seconds) for artifacts: prompt, response, request_log, metric
API and Console allow org-admins to set immutable guardrails per-tenant and optionally lock overrides for sub-routes
Anomaly detection hook documented: service can call /v1/retention/snapshots with a trigger-id and bounded retention TTL for snapshot artifacts
Snapshot artifacts are packaged with metadata, signed by platform HSM key, and uploaded to tenant-configured evidence destination (S3 or customer webhook)
Console displays snapshot events with link to evidence package, reason, and TTL enforced; webhook delivered to configured endpoint within 30s of snapshot creation
E2E test demonstrating that a sub-route cannot set TTL outside tenant guardrail when tenant guardrail is locked
Operational metrics: snapshot_success_rate >= 98%, avg_snapshot_latency <= 400ms (for small bundles <10KB)
work_items: PM: finalize tenant guardrail UX copy and default presets
ENG: API schema and persistence for tenant guardrails (DB migration + validation)
ENG: snapshot service endpoint + signer integration with HSM
ENG: uploader component supporting S3 and webhook destinations
ENG: console UI to configure guardrails and view snapshot events
Design: compact evidence artifact format and metadata schema
QA: test matrix for TTL enforcement and snapshot scenarios
Docs: public API docs and runbook for tenants to configure evidence destinations
tech_notes: Decision: store tenant guardrails as a separate DB table keyed by tenant_id to reduce policy evaluation latency; evaluate 2-column index on (tenant_id, artifact_type)

Trade-off: real-time snapshot hook calls will be sync for small bundles but fall back to async queue for larger exports to avoid blocking caller; initial scope only supports small synchronous snapshots (<100KB)
Security: use existing HSM signing key for package signing. Private deployments will use customer-managed KMS when configured (explicit flag).
Compatibility: Guardrails are evaluated in the routing layer pre-request; if a requested TTL violates tenant min/max then request is rejected with 400 + explanation header 'X-Retention-Policy-Reason'
Observability: emit metrics snapshot_requests_total, snapshot_errors, snapshot_latency_ms; tag by tenant_id and route for downstream billing/forensics
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic (min/max enforcement across artifact types)
Integration tests: simulate anomaly trigger -> create snapshot -> verify signed artifact uploaded to mock S3 and webhook endpoint
Regression: verify existing per-route TTLs continue to apply for tenants without guardrails
Load test: create 1k snapshot events across 200 tenants over 1m to validate queueing fallback and observe latency percentiles
rollout_plan: Week 1 (canary): Deploy API + DB migration behind feature flag for 5 pilot tenants; observe enforcement and snapshot flows
Week 2: Enable Console controls for org-admins in pilot orgs; gather feedback from pilot security teams
Week 3: Gradual rollout to all tenants with 1% increments per day; monitor snapshot_success_rate and errors
Fallback: feature flag to disable automatic snapshot uploads globally; manual evidence export remains available
